;Armed conflicts and attacks
*[[2019 Ménaka attack]]
**Gunmen [[mass murder|kill 53]] [[Malian Armed Forces|soldiers]] and a civilian in a [[mass shooting]] in [[Ménaka Region]], [[Mali]]. [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-mali-security/mali-says-at-least-15-soldiers-killed-in-militant-attack-idUSKBN1XB4W7 (Reuters)]

;Business and economy
*[[Google]] purchases [[activity tracker]] company [[Fitbit]] for [[US$]]2.1 billion, in an attempt to break into the [[digital health]] and [[smartwatch]] markets. [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-fitbit-m-a-alphabet/google-taps-fitness-tracker-market-with-2-1-billion-bid-for-fitbit-idUSKBN1XB47G (Reuters)]
*The [[Committee on Foreign Investment in the United States]] launches a national security review of [[TikTok]]-owner [[ByteDance]]'s US$1 billion purchase of [[social media]] platform [[Musical.ly]]. [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-tiktok-cfius-exclusive/exclusive-u-s-opens-national-security-investigation-into-tiktok-sources-idUSKBN1XB4IL (Reuters)]
*[[Governor of California|California Governor]] [[Gavin Newsom]] issues a statement calling on the [[Pacific Gas and Electric Company]], the state's largest utility company, to find a "consensual resolution" to its bankruptcy case, threatening a state takeover if an agreement cannot be reached. PG&E [[Pacific Gas and Electric Company#2019 bankruptcy|filed for Chapter 11 bankruptcy]] in January in response to lawsuits pertaining to wildfires caused by PG&E's equipment. [https://www.npr.org/2019/11/01/775621356/calif-governor-seeks-to-jumpstart-pg-e-bankruptcy-talks-threatens-state-takeover (NPR)]
;Disasters and accidents
*A [[Grumman OV-1 Mohawk]] crashes at an [[air show]] in [[Stuart, Florida]], killing the pilot. [https://www.wptv.com/news/region-martin-county/stuart/plane-crash-at-stuart-air-show?BBBB&fbclid=IwAR0GEnLG2jzi6HcfYPoNEqKQawjmcRxLoz_7b-PvTi7MP4hkvGc99Re4xkw (WPTV-TV)]
*In [[Tottenham]], [[London]], a 1-year-old boy dies after falling from a ninth-floor [[council flat]] window with a faulty handle in a [[tower block]]. The boy's mother had urged the [[Haringey London Borough Council]] to fix the window for two months, a neighbour says. Critics say the death is the latest in a number of incidents suggesting problems with the ways in which [[public housing]] is managed in the country. [https://www.thesun.co.uk/news/10257568/baby-boy-fall-death-tottenham-london-news/ (''The Sun'')]

;Law and crime
*[[Crime in France]]
**A gunman [[mass shooting|shoots and injures]] six people at a bar in [[Marseille]], [[France]]. The gunman is still at large. [https://www.euronews.com/2019/10/31/six-injured-after-shooting-at-a-bar-in-marseille-police-source (Euronews)]
*[[2019 Samoa assassination plot]]
**A man who had pled guilty to [[conspiracy to murder|conspiracy to assassinate]] the [[Prime Minister of Samoa]], and was due to be sentenced today, has changed his plea from guilty to not-guilty. [https://www.rnz.co.nz/international/pacific-news/402296/man-who-admitted-conspiracy-to-kill-samoan-pm-to-change-plea (Radio New Zealand)]
*[[Irish people|Irish]] [[Mixed martial arts|mixed-martial artist]] [[Conor McGregor]] is convicted for assaulting a man in a [[Drimnagh]] pub in April, and is fined [[Euro|€]]1,000. [https://www.bbc.com/news/world-europe-50260195 (BBC News)]
*[[Essex lorry deaths]]
**Earlier statements about the victims being of Chinese nationality are repudiated. [[Essex Police]] say all victims were Vietnamese. [https://www.bbc.com/news/uk-england-essex-50268939 (BBC News)]

;Politics and elections
*[[2020 Democratic Party presidential primaries]]
**Former [[Texas]] [[United States House of Representatives|representative]] [[Beto O'Rourke]] drops out of the presidential primaries. [https://www.vox.com/policy-and-politics/2019/11/1/20944401/beto-o-rourke-presidential-bid-end-2020-democratic-primary (''Vox'')]
*Tens of thousands of protestors, mostly consisting of supporters of the conservative [[Jamiat Ulema-e-Islam (F)|Jamiat Ulema-i-Islam-Fazal]], march in [[Islamabad]] demanding the resignation of [[Prime Minister of Pakistan|Prime Minister]] [[Imran Khan]] by Sunday. [[Pakistan Armed Forces|The army]] announces later in the evening that they will continue to support [[Imran Khan ministry|the elected government]]. [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-pakistan-politics-protests/pakistan-army-says-supports-elected-government-amid-major-protest-idUSKBN1XC064?il=0 (Reuters)]
*[[2020 United States presidential election]], [[2020 Iowa Democratic caucuses]]
**A [[The New York Times|New York Times]]-[[Siena College]] poll finds there is no clear [[Democratic Party (United States)|Democratic Party]] frontrunner among voters in [[Iowa]] three months away from the [[2020 Iowa Democratic caucuses]]. [[United States Senate|Senator]] [[Elizabeth Warren]] leads the poll with 22 percent, followed by [[United States Senate|Senator]] [[Bernie Sanders]] with 19 percent. [[South Bend, Indiana|South Bend]], [[Indiana]], Mayor [[Pete Buttigieg]] holds 18 percent in a rise to third place, while former [[Vice President of the United States|Vice President]] [[Joe Biden]], seen by many to be the frontrunner for his party's nomination, comes in fourth place with 17 percent. [https://www.cnn.com/2019/11/01/politics/new-york-times-2020-democrats-poll-november/index.html?fbclid=IwAR2pqLMjyoR4BAx4NoJb7A84R3mdcndL5hXIcI353PKv6V6c3F64rKV9A-M (CNN)]
